scope: Researcher-constructed standards-grounded grouping; not expert validation or official CICIoT-to-CAPEC annotation.

rules.basis: Normal traffic has no attack-pattern annotation.
rules.limitation: Benign group remains fixed in the wrong control.

rules.basis: Labels explicitly name TCP or TCP flags in flooding traffic.
rules.limitation: TCP flooding does not establish bandwidth exhaustion versus connection-state exhaustion. DoS/DDoS is not used to infer T1499 versus T1498.

rules.basis: Explicit UDP flood or UDPPlain generator; malware name does not define a separate mechanism.
rules.limitation: No assertion of reflection or amplification; distributed sources not inferred from aggregate features.

rules.basis: ICMP flooding is explicitly named.
rules.limitation: Does not establish a specific ICMP message subtype or a production impact.

rules.basis: Label explicitly describes fragmented TCP ACK flooding; grouped by fragmentation with other fragmented floods.
rules.limitation: CAPEC-494 describes filter evasion, not this label's established denial-of-service mechanism. It is a related candidate, not an exact annotation; CAPEC-125 supports only general flooding.

rules.basis: UDP fragmentation resource consumption is explicitly named.
rules.limitation: No claim that every feature row records reassembly or measured victim exhaustion.

rules.basis: ICMP fragmentation is explicitly named.
rules.limitation: Crash versus resource-consumption outcome is not resolved by the label.

rules.basis: HTTP request flooding consumes service/application resources.
rules.limitation: ATT&CK T1499 is a related resource-effect concept, not a per-flow finding.

rules.basis: Slowloris retains HTTP sessions and depletes server connection resources.
rules.limitation: Grouped with HTTP flood by resource mechanism; low-rate session holding differs from high-rate HTTP requests.

rules.basis: Labels establish flooding but do not share an exact protocol-specific CAPEC child.
rules.limitation: Does not infer spoofing, reflection, encapsulated payload, or a specific ATT&CK subtechnique merely from a generator name.

rules.basis: Probes determine whether hosts are present.
rules.limitation: No exact probe protocol inferred.

rules.basis: Sweeps probe host liveness; ICMP echo is a related ping implementation.
rules.limitation: CAPEC-292 is primary; CAPEC-285 is conditional because ping can use non-ICMP probes.

rules.basis: Active OS scanning fingerprints responses to probes.
rules.limitation: Does not use deprecated CAPEC-311 or claim passive fingerprinting.

rules.basis: Probing determines remote port state.
rules.limitation: No SYN versus connect versus UDP scan subtype inferred.

rules.basis: Scanning identifies vulnerable software or configurations.
rules.limitation: ATT&CK T1595.002 is related but pre-compromise context is not established by a network label.

rules.basis: Untrusted input changes interpreted commands; CAPEC-248 is general command injection.
rules.limitation: CAPEC-88 is conditional on OS-shell execution and is not inferred solely from CommandInjection.

rules.basis: Untrusted input changes the intended SQL statement.
rules.limitation: No database engine or successful compromise inferred.

rules.basis: Injected malicious script is served to a browser.
rules.limitation: No stored/reflected/DOM subtype inferred.

rules.basis: A malware/backdoor label is compatible with malicious logic in a deployed component.
rules.limitation: Insertion path, execution, persistence and remote-access technique are unresolved. This is an explicit fallback bucket, not an official mechanism category.

rules.basis: Adversary-in-browser is a related browser-control pattern.
rules.limitation: The label alone does not demonstrate traffic manipulation required by CAPEC-662 or session-cookie theft. Kept in unresolved fallback, not assigned T1185 as fact.

rules.basis: Web-shell upload is a candidate attack pattern for a malicious upload.
rules.limitation: Uploading_Attack alone does not prove a remotely executable web shell. Kept in unresolved fallback; candidate is not asserted ground truth.

rules.basis: Dictionary words are tried as password guesses.
rules.limitation: Does not equate dictionary guessing to password spraying or credential stuffing.

rules.basis: Forged DNS responses redirect requested resources.
rules.limitation: Does not assert cache poisoning or credential interception as the observed outcome.

rules.basis: ARP spoofing permits adversary-in-the-middle traffic interception/redirection.
rules.limitation: ATT&CK ARP Cache Poisoning supports the named mechanism; no specific data theft outcome inferred.
